valid_ceiling.citation: Wiktionary files Arabic entries at the unvocalized page title (Wiktionary:About_Arabic), so the wikipron input column carries no harakat; folding short vowels out of the gold IPA before rescoring gives this consonant-only floor. See this file's notes, 'MEASURED UNDECIDABLE-INPUT CEILING'.

Wikipron gold marks the Bats voiceless lateral fricative /ɬ/ and voiceless pharyngeal fricative /ħ/ with a supplementary IPA modifier apostrophe on top of plain Georgian letters (ლʻ, ჰʼ), a scholarly disambiguation the practical Georgian Mkhedruli orthography does not make -- confirmed against Holisky & Gagua (1994)'s grapheme table, which lists no such distinct letters. Folding /ɬ/->/l/, /ħ/->/h/ out of both sides drops wikipron/bbl PER from 0.2790 to 0.2635 (n=414); measured on fix/bbl-nasalization.

Scored as-is (this spec's fixed inherent_vowel_final="") the row is 0.2395 PER. Stripping the final vowel character from BOTH hypothesis and gold whenever the orthographic word ends in a bare consonant letter (neutralising the remaining deletion/raising choice on both sides) measures 0.2274 -- this isolates what is left of the inherent-vowel phenomenon from the conjunct/যা-phala and other residual errors; see the notes field for the underlying counts.

valid_ceiling.folded: the /r/~/ʁ/ realisation difference, contingent vowel nasalisation, and the close/open ⟨e⟩ contrast
valid_ceiling.citation: Press, I. (1986), A Grammar of Modern Breton, Mouton de Gruyter. p. 34, section 3.2.1.3 'The Laterals and Vibrants': "The vibrant(s) are pronounced as an alveolar trill or as a uvular fricative, depending on local usage. The overall tendency has been for the uvular to replace the trill, probably under the influence of standard French" — [r] and [ʁ] are two local realisations of one phoneme, so the choice between them is a transcription decision, not a fact about the word. p. 21, section 2.4 'Nasality', on a vowel nasalised by a following nasal consonant: "This is a clear case where individual dialects and words must decide", and "A possible proposal might be to allocate a contingently nasal vowel to the oral vowel phoneme, and the nasal element to the nasal consonant phoneme" — which is the analysis this spec implements, since ⟨Vn⟩ outside the ⟨añ eñ iñ oñ uñ euñ⟩ digraphs yields an oral vowel plus /n/. p. 29, section 3.1.1.3: "there seems to be no clear way, through quantity or through following consonants/silence, of constraining the close and open e", and the two are assigned to separate phonemes /e/ and /ɛ/ — both written ⟨e⟩ in peurunvan, so the contrast is not recoverable from the input. Folding all three on both sides of the same 803 scored words leaves PER 0.1726; folded one at a time they give 0.2616 (rhotic), 0.2682 (nasalisation) and 0.2593 (⟨e⟩) against the 0.3073 as-scored.

Standard Ewe orthography marks tone only where disambiguation requires it (Ansre 1961; Capo 1991); raw PER of 0.4445 against the WikiPron ewe_latn_broad gold (which transcribes a tone on every vowel) drops to 0.008 once tone diacritics are folded out of both sides -- see the `notes` field above for the full measurement (245 of 247 spellings match exactly after folding).

Re-measured after fixing the enm ⟨y⟩/⟨x⟩/⟨ð⟩ grapheme gaps (see spec notes, y-grapheme fix). As-scored PER (n=6466, broad+strip_stress, enm_latn_broad.tsv) moved from the prior 0.2981 (measured against the defective spec that dropped ⟨y⟩ silently) to 0.2620 with the fixed spec. Folding the vowel-length mark ː out of both hypothesis and gold (same predicate as before: the gold disagrees with itself about vowel length within 1403 of 6466 headwords, e.g. Irish -> iriʃ / iːriʃ) now measures 0.2163 -- below the 0.25 production threshold. The prior 0.2538 folded figure was measured against the ⟨y⟩-dropping spec and undercounted correct segments the fixed spec now produces; it is superseded by this figure, not additive to it. This row is now input-limited by the gold's internal vowel-length disagreement rather than by a spec defect.

The wikipron ha gold's IPA column is fully marked for tone and length while the orthographic column is stripped of both (Module:ha-IPA output); measured over 1857 scored items, baseline PER 0.5340 drops to 0.0223 (89.1% exact match) once both tone and length are folded out of both sides -- folding tone alone gives 0.1690 and length alone gives 0.4565, which must not be conflated with the combined figure. See docs/languages/ha.md.

valid_ceiling.folded: four-way pitch-accent diacritics (rising/falling x long/short) + vowel-length mark
valid_ceiling.citation: As-scored PER (n=26469, broad+strip_stress convention) is 0.3000. Landau, Lončarić, Horga & Škarić 1995 (JIPA 25(2):83-86, doi:10.1017/S002510030000520X), p.85, describe the four-way word-accent contrast (long rising, short rising, long falling, short falling) and state the accent marks they use 'are not part of the usual orthography, but are used to mark the accents in specialized linguistic works'; standard Croatian spelling never writes them. Measured in the gold: 95.4% of wikipron/hbs_latn_broad entries carry a pitch-accent diacritic (caron/circumflex/grave/acute) on a vowel and 53.5% carry the length mark ː, against 0% of the orthographic input forms carrying either. Folding the accent diacritics out of both sides alone takes PER to 0.2269; folding length alone takes it to 0.2524; folding both together reaches 0.1733. Syllabic /r/ is written in the gold with the IPA syllabicity mark directly on r (e.g. prst -> p r̩̂ s t), not with an epenthetic schwa, and the spec's existing syllabic-r rule already targets that representation, so no schwa-insertion rule was needed or added. Measured this session against the wikipron/hr (hbs_latn_broad.tsv) gold; not itself sourced as a target number.

Standard Gikuyu orthography marks neither tone/downstep nor vowel length (Englebretson 2015, A Basic Sketch Grammar of Gikuyu, pp. xi, 9), both of which the wikipron gold transcribes; measured over the same 1025 scored words as the row above, baseline PER 0.3914 drops to 0.0523 folding tone alone, 0.3843 folding length alone, and 0.0344 folding both together -- see orthography2ipa/data/ki.json's valid_ceiling entry and scripts/fold_ki_notation.py.

Re-measured against the current spec (post #1366's short-⟨a⟩ backness fix, raw PER 0.3048, n=10169). Scandinavian quantity is one contrast written two ways -- a long vowel XOR a geminate consonant -- so both notations of it are folded together on both hypothesis and gold: the vowel length mark ː is stripped, and any run of an identical letter (the doubled-letter notation _expand_consonant_length already canonicalises consonant gemination to) is collapsed to one. That fold alone moves PER to 0.2096, clearing the 0.25 production threshold. Folding the ¹/² toneme digits on top makes no further difference (0.2096, unchanged) because this gold carries zero toneme digits, confirming the toneme fold remains a no-op for ipadict specifically, as recorded when this ceiling was first measured pre-fix in #1361 (then 0.3397 raw / 0.2477 folded, both stale after #1366 moved the underlying vowel rule).

Re-measured against the current spec (raw PER 0.3654, n=2725, up from 0.3471 pre-#1366 -- see the notes field for the unresolved front/back split behind that regression). The same length+gemination fold used for ipadict moves this row to 0.3039; folding the ¹/² toneme digits on top (this gold, unlike ipadict, carries them) moves it further to 0.2995. That does NOT clear the 0.25 production threshold, so this row stays open rather than proved input-limited: something beyond notation, plausibly the front/back ⟨a⟩ split documented in the notes field, still accounts for roughly three tenths of the row's segments.

As-scored PER (n=1564, broad+strip_stress convention) is 0.3119. Downing & Mtenje 2017 (The Phonology of Chichewa, OUP) §2.1 state that Chichewa contrasts lexical high and low tone but that 'tone is not indicated in Chichewa orthography'; the spec's notes already record this as deliberately unmodelled. Measured in the wikipron/nya_latn_broad gold: 731/1624 entries (45.0%) carry a combining acute-accent tone mark on a vowel or syllabic nasal, against 0/1624 orthographic headwords marking it (the two NFD hits on plain ŵ/Ŵ are the orthographic letter itself, not a tone diacritic, and were excluded). 59 of the 1564 unique headwords recur in the gold with more than one tone pattern for the identical spelling, direct evidence the orthography underdetermines tone. Folding the acute tone mark out of both hypothesis and gold (grave/circumflex/caron were checked and do not occur in this gold) takes PER to 0.2604. No vowel-length mark (ː or ˑ) occurs anywhere in this gold's 1624 entries, so a length fold was tried and made no difference — a negative result: this gold's broad transcription convention does not record the penultimate lengthening Downing & Mtenje describe, so there is nothing for a length rule to be measured against here. Measured this session against the wikipron/nya_latn_broad.tsv gold; not itself sourced as a target number.

valid_ceiling.folded: glottal stop + unwritten-stress vowel quality (a/ə, i/ɪ, u/ʊ)
valid_ceiling.citation: As-scored PER (n=860, broad+strip_stress, pam_latn_broad.tsv) is 0.2861, matching the committed board row. Two unwritten phenomena drive it. First, the word-final glottal stop: Sulat Wawa never marks it in this gold's 926 raw headwords (0 carry an apostrophe or any other mark), while 108 of the 860 scored gold pronunciations carry ʔ -- the spec's own notes already record the glottal stop as 'phonemic but usually unwritten'. Second, Kapampangan stress is phonemic and lexical, not marked in ordinary spelling (Forman 1971, Kapampangan Grammar Notes; summarised at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapampangan_language, which cites Forman 1971 pp.28-29 for the stress facts): 48 headwords recur in this crowd-scraped gold with mutually incompatible readings for the identical spelling (e.g. Guagua -> ɡwaɡwə vs wawəʔ), direct evidence the orthography underdetermines which syllable is stressed. Under that lexical, unrecoverable stress assignment, /a/ centralizes to [ə] when unstressed (757 of 1253 scored a/ə tokens) against [a] when stressed, and the close vowels /i u/ lax to [ɪ ʊ] under the same unstressed condition (153 and 124 tokens respectively, against 0 orthographic marking of stress anywhere in the 926 headwords). A positional heuristic -- treating only the word-final vowel as stressed, the rest as reduced -- was tried and only narrows raw PER to 0.2351, a negative result: the gold's own conflicting readings for identical spellings show the alternation is lexical rather than positional, so no such rule was added. Folding the glottal stop and the a/ə, i/ɪ, u/ʊ alternation out of both hypothesis and gold together measures 0.0843 -- well under the 0.25 production threshold, so the row is input-limited rather than defective. The gold's plain ⟨e⟩ notation (0 of 926 entries write ɛ, 119 write e, for the mid front vowel this spec's Forman-sourced phonemic analysis assigns /ɛ/) is a separate, UNFOLDED notation-convention mismatch: the vowel letter IS written, only its exact IPA symbol choice differs by convention, so it is documented in docs/gold_defects.md rather than counted toward this ceiling.

shn_mymr_broad.tsv scored as-is (after the ိူ/ို compound-vowel and ႀ=θ grapheme fixes below) is 0.3057 PER over 2607 rows. Unlike Thai/Lao, Shan spells tone with explicit, unambiguous tone-mark letters rather than computing it from consonant class, so the Thai tone-PLACEMENT fold (move the mark to a fixed position, keep identity/order) barely moves the number -- 0.3040, essentially unchanged -- confirming that prior does not transfer here. Folding tone IDENTITY out entirely on both sides (this spec emits all 6 tone marks; scripts/fold_shn_notation.py) gives 0.2547, just above the 0.25 production threshold. Folding vowel length ⟨ː⟩ as well (a notation dimension the gold transcribes inconsistently in some rows) gives 0.2777. The residual above this ceiling is a real, uninvestigated segmental gap (word-boundary/compounding errors in multi-syllable entries), not a tone-notation artifact.

valid_ceiling.folded: tonal-accent diacritics (acute/grave/circumflex) + stress placement + vowel length + e/o mid-vowel quality + syllabic-r epenthetic schwa
valid_ceiling.citation: As-scored PER (n=5139, broad+strip_stress convention) is 0.3284. 97.7% of gold entries carry a Slovene dictionary-style pitch-accent mark (acute/grave/circumflex) that standard orthography never writes -- Sustarsic, Komar & Petek 1995 (JIPA 25(2):86-90, doi:10.1017/S0025100300005211) report that stress placement is 'not predictable' from spelling, and that in their own careful phonetic transcription the acute/circumflex pitch-accent contrast is left unmarked because it is 'seldom lexically distinctive' and varies between speakers, even though vowel length and stress position are marked despite the redundancy. Folding the tone/stress diacritics out of both sides (they encode information the orthography cannot signal) takes PER to 0.2284. Folding the e/o mid-vowel quality contrast on top (the same source reports 'e' represents [e, ɛ, ə] and 'o' represents [o, ɔ] with no orthographic mark, already modelled here as a graphemes candidate list) adds almost nothing on its own (0.3284 -> 0.3282 alone) but reaches 0.1941 combined with the tone/stress fold. Folding a syllabic-r epenthetic schwa (er/re <-> r alternations) on top reaches 0.1901. Folding word-final l -> w l-vocalisation (already a candidate allophone in this spec) on top of all the above made no further difference (0.1901 unchanged) -- a negative result showing the l~w choice is not a current PER driver, so no new rule was added for it. Measured this session against the wikipron/sl gold; not itself sourced as a target number.

vox_communis is an Epitran-derived, non-qualifying gold (directional signal only, cannot gate a regression or tier promotion) whose Epitran pipeline writes the tone letter on the nucleus rather than syllable-finally; scored as-is the row is 0.4318 PER. Moving the tone letter to the end of the transcription on both sides, neutralising placement while keeping tone identity, measures 0.2295 -- this isolates the notation mismatch from a phonological one; see the notes field and docs/languages/th.md.

WikiPron writes the Chao tone letter after the whole syllable, matching this spec's tone_rules output position; scored as-is the row is 0.1881 PER. Moving the tone letter to the end of the transcription on both hypothesis and gold sides (neutralising placement while keeping tone identity and order) measures 0.1713 -- see the notes field and docs/languages/th.md for the full measurement.

vox_communis is a Common Voice force-aligned, Epitran-derived gold (a scored competitor's lexicon, directional signal only -- cannot gate a regression or tier promotion). As-scored PER with the corrected /e̝/ /o̝/ vowel values is 0.3953 (n=2271). Folding the gold's own conventions out of both sides cumulatively (see fold_tn_notation.py, broad-normalized): the gold's literal /ɪ/ /ʊ/ vowel-notation convention takes it to 0.3105; the implosive-b convention to 0.2846; the kg fold is a no-op, confirming 0.2846; and dropping the ejective marker -- a symbol this gold's phone tier has no way to encode at all -- takes it to 0.2066. Dropping the aspiration marker was also tried and made the score worse (0.2871), a negative result not included in this fold. Measured, not sourced; see the notes field for the full chain.

Xhosa tone is phonemic but never written, and this spec emits no tone diacritics, so the raw PER of 0.3779 against the kaikki Xhosa gold (887 scored entries) measures tone marks the hypothesis could never reproduce, not a spelling defect. Folding tone (combining acute, grave, circumflex, caron, and the grave-acute-grave contour mark) out of the gold IPA only -- one-sided, since the hypothesis side already carries none -- drops PER to 0.1519 and moves exact match from 2.8% to 41.2%; 841 of the 892 kaikki entries carry at least one tone diacritic. Measured against kaikki's Xhosa dump this session, not sourced from a published figure.
